description_en: Julius Caesar was Augustus great-uncle (mother uncle). Caesar named Octavius as his principal heir in his will (45 BCE), creating a testamentary father-son relationship.
Co-triumvir (43–33 BCE), then rival and enemy in civil war. Relationship progressed from alliance to competition to open war, culminating in the Battle of Actium (31 BCE).
note: Antony was also married to Octavian's sister Octavia (40–32 BCE)

description_en: Co-triumvir (43–36 BCE), then sidelined. Removed from power in 36 BCE after attempting to claim Sicily.
Enemy; Octavian declared war on Cleopatra (not Antony) in 32 BCE as a propaganda tactic to frame the conflict as a foreign war.
Lifelong friend and most capable general. Commanded the naval victories at Naulochus (36 BCE) and Actium (31 BCE). Married Augustus daughter Julia (21 BCE).
Wife from 38 BCE until his death in 14 CE (51 years). Powerful political advisor.
Only biological child (by Scribonia, born 39 BCE). Exiled 2 BCE for adultery.
Stepson (Livia son), adopted as heir in 4 CE after the deaths of Gaius and Lucius Caesar. Succeeded Augustus as princeps.
Octavian initially allied with Cicero against Antony in 44–43 BCE. Cicero was proscribed and killed under the Triumvirate on 7 December 43 BCE.
note: Relationship evolved from political ally to victim of the proscriptions that Augustus co-authorized
